gaps.note: Commercial break edit, possible loss of dialogue.

stage_a.note: Very strong positive expression; he is upbeat, smiling, and passionate about helping dogs.
Very animated, strong gestures, and clear passion for the science and its potential.
Approaches the panel warmly, hands out puppies, and maintains a very friendly demeanor.

venture.description: Stem cell banking and regenerative medicine for pets, allowing owners to bank stem cells during routine spay/neuter procedures.
venture.note: Service includes banking the cells and developing therapeutics.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces himself, his company Gallant, and hands out puppies to the panel to demonstrate the patients they will help.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reacts with surprise and amusement as the Grim Reaper enters the set.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes with the Grim Reaper to move along and not touch his puppy.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Jokes that her puppy does not want to go with the Grim Reaper.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes to the puppy that he tried to buy the Reaper out but got no deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that his puppy wanted a royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that he is turning into Robert while holding the dog.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains how stem cells can treat age-related ailments and states his ask of $500,000 for 2% of the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that the pitch is not going to end well.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks about the company's sales given the high valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they have a therapeutics division developing medicines and a consumer banking division launching in three weeks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Jokes that he knows how this is going to end.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks the founder to tell them his history.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shares his background of starting a dog sitting platform that grew massively and merged with a competitor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks for the name of the founder's previous company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States his previous company was called DogVacay, which is now Rover.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks about the founder's background training.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he was a neuroscience major, hired top minds, and secured four key patents.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that he has patents.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms briefly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what the patents cover technically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains how stem cells regenerate tissue and how they patented isolating them from reproductive tissue during spay/neuter.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that he wants to use the stem cells for himself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Recommends he do it, noting it changed his own life.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Jokes that he would have to be neutered first.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Challenges the science, stating that if a simple injection worked, injuries would never matter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Deflects the challenge by saying it sounds like a great dream.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks why, if it worked, anyone with a decent doctor isn't already doing it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Defends the premise, noting that while not standard for humans yet, there is a whole world of animal research.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks how much it costs the consumer to get the kit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they charge $95 a year to store the stem cells.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that paying $95 a year gets the kit for free.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms and explains that they send the kit directly to the veterinarian.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if the veterinarian makes money from the process.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms it is a revenue stream for vets, who make about $100.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Points out that they instantly lose money on initial acquisition by paying the vet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes the point.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks how much it costs to do the extraction.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the cost of the kit and shipping is about $275.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if that cost includes what they pay the vet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that it is plus what they pay the vet, though most vets do it for free.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks for the business's burn rate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they are burning about $400,000 a month, mostly on R&D.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if there are any other investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they have raised a total of $10 million to fund the business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks for the valuation on the last funding round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the valuation was $25 million, the same as his ask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks how much money they will have to raise since they don't have marketing money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Estimates they will have to raise another $25 million in 2021.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Expresses anxiety about the high acquisition costs and losing money on every sale.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Repeats the concern that losing money on every sale will sink the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Adds that they will not have the cash flow to support the model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Argues they are well capitalized and have a very good investor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rebuts that they are not well capitalized because they can't sell anything.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Compares them to 23andMe, which makes money on every kit, and worries about the long recapture time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes that it takes a little while to recapture the costs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Jokes that if Anne is nervous, he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Appeals to Daymond's love of pets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Exits the deal, reiterating that Anne's nervousness concerns him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for hope on how the $275 cost will go down, as the consumer business is a money sink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Suggests raising prices.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees that raising prices to $399 is not a bad idea to stop hemorrhaging money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they lowered barriers to entry initially to create word of mouth and get vets on board.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Supports the scaling strategy, noting 23andMe launched at a high price and lowered it at scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes that at scale there might be a better pricing structure.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Hypes his own creativity and introduces himself as Mr. Wonderful before making an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Makes two alternative offers involving options or a royalty to bridge the valuation gap.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells the founder to think about it while the others natter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Compliments the creativity of the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that Kevin would be a great partner.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Exits the deal, stating he believes in stem cells but thinks the business model isn't figured out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Expresses belief in the long-term potential and suggests a partnership with Lori for direct-to-consumer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Makes a joint offer with Lori for $500,000 for 8% of the company.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mocks the 8% equity ask.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Expresses a strong desire to work with them but notes his responsibility to protect his employees' equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Pressures the founder to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters Anne and Lori's offer, asking if they would do 4%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Revises their offer to 5%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the revised offer.

Creative structure to account for valuation.
